result.title: OpenKAGE: Open-Ended Lifelong Learning in the Open World via Knowledge-Sharing Agent-Group Evolution
result.summary: Building autonomous agents that continually explore open worlds and acquire new capabilities through experience is a long-standing aspiration in artificial intelligence. Existing research often pursues lifelong learning within predefined tasks, curricula, or objectives, with self-improvement largely confined to individual agents. We introduce OpenKAGE, an agent-group evolution framework for open-ended lifelong learning. Within this framework, agents autonomously explore open worlds and continually acquire new capabilities by accumulating and reusing knowledge from their own interactions and the experience of others. OpenKAGE builds on two key mechanisms: (1) a two-layer knowledge representation, with a memory layer for situated memories and an experience layer for transferable experience and skills that retains the applicability conditions needed for reuse; and (2) a knowledge-sharing mechanism that semantically consolidates textual experience into a continuously evolving shared knowledge graph, while executable skills are shared verbatim. In Minecraft, OpenKAGE supports open-ended lifelong learning, enabling agent groups to sustain exploration and reach advanced technological milestones. Furthermore, the accumulated knowledge can be transferred to a newly initialized agent group on a different backbone model, improving its survival and exploration progress.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 OpenKAGE，一个在 Minecraft 开放世界中做终身学习的智能体群体演化框架：用两层知识表示区分情境记忆与带「适用条件」的可迁移经验，并通过将文本经验语义整合成共享知识图谱、技能原样共享的机制，让智能体群体持续积累与复用能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「情境记忆 vs 带适用条件的可迁移经验」分层，可供核查 latent 内部状态是否显式保留任务必要的适用条件与复用边界，跨智能体经验共享也可类比推理轨迹的监督与贡献分配；但该文属具身智能体终身学习，与视觉推理主线的直接联系仍需判断。
